title: Building & Testing Networks
description: Study registering parameters and submodules, loss functions and output contracts, dropout and normalization behavior, and testing a network before scaling. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Registering parameters and submodules
lessons.description: Build a three-layer stack and verify every intended trainable tensor appears in the parameter list and state dictionary.
lessons.conceptOverview: nn.Module tracks assigned parameters and child modules so state dictionaries, optimizers, and device transfers can discover them. Plain Python containers do not register their contents in the same way as ModuleList or ModuleDict. A network can run a forward pass while accidentally omitting parameters from optimization.
lessons.whyItMatters: Use registered module containers for learnable layers created dynamically.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A list of hidden layers stored in a plain list may not appear in model.parameters(). A ModuleList registers those layers while allowing a custom forward loop.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Build a three-layer stack and verify every intended trainable tensor appears in the parameter list and state dictionary. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

commonMistakes: Any Python list of layers is automatically registered by nn.Module.

lessons.title: Loss functions and output contracts
lessons.description: Specify output shape, target shape, dtype, and loss for binary classification, multiclass classification, and regression.
lessons.conceptOverview: Match the model output to the loss definition. Multiclass cross entropy commonly takes raw class logits and class-index targets; applying softmax first is usually the wrong interface. Binary tasks may use a numerically stable logits-based loss. Inspect reduction and masking so the scalar loss represents the intended examples.
lessons.whyItMatters: Choose the loss from label semantics and its documented input contract.

lessons.title: Dropout and normalization behavior
lessons.description: Run a fixed batch repeatedly in train and eval modes. Separate random variation from a systematic shift in predictions.
lessons.conceptOverview: Dropout changes activations during training and is disabled in evaluation mode. Batch normalization uses different statistics in training and evaluation, so small or shifted batches can affect behavior. Layer normalization uses within-example features instead. Switching modes does not fix mismatched preprocessing or distribution shift.
lessons.whyItMatters: Check layer behavior and preprocessing before attributing every discrepancy to randomness.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A prediction that changes between repeated evaluation requests may indicate dropout was left active. A stable but biased result may instead reflect incorrect normalization statistics.

lessons.title: Testing a network before scaling
lessons.description: Create a tiny-batch diagnostic report with initial loss, final loss, gradient norms, and prediction accuracy.
lessons.conceptOverview: A useful model test verifies observable behavior, not only that forward executes. Check output shapes, finite losses, nonzero gradients where expected, and whether a tiny dataset can be overfit. Compare trainable parameter counts with the design. These checks localize basic implementation failures before expensive training.
lessons.whyItMatters: Overfit a small clean batch to test whether the training path can learn.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A classifier that cannot fit eight clean labeled examples may have a label, optimization, or architecture bug. More data is unlikely to repair a disconnected gradient path.
